cldap_rootdse_disclosure.title: CLDAP rootDSE Information Disclosure
cldap_rootdse_disclosure.description: The host responds to Connectionless LDAP (CLDAP) rootDSE queries on UDP/389. The rootDSE entry discloses domain naming context, DNS hostname, server name, and other directory metadata to anyone reaching the port.
cldap_rootdse_disclosure.impact: Reveals the AD domain DN (e.g., `DC=corp,DC=example,DC=local`) and DC hostname. Attackers use this for AD reconnaissance — feeding the info into BloodHound, ldapsearch, or kerbrute follow-ups.
cldap_rootdse_disclosure.remediation: CLDAP is typically only used by AD clients during discovery. If this host is internal-only, restrict UDP/389 at the firewall. If external CLDAP access is required (rare), disable rootDSE response via the AD LDAP policy (requires careful testing — some AD client workflows depend on it).
cldap_rootdse_disclosure.evidence_template: CLDAP rootDSE query against {{host}}:389 returned defaultNamingContext: {{default_naming_context}}
